provenance: Candidate wording supplied in the Experiment 38 protocol; authored as a GPT-6 literature synthesis, not a GPT-4 API response, clinician-authenticated statement, or confirmed single-edge ASD effect.

indexing.corr_index: 0-based position among the 256 selected FC features
indexing.input_index: 64 + corr_index in the unchanged 320D processed input

hypotheses.asd: ASD hypothesis: Thalamic coupling with the superior or middle temporal cortex may be atypically elevated relative to comparable typical development; this is a variable, non-diagnostic candidate.
hypotheses.td: TD hypothesis: Thalamic coupling with the superior or middle temporal cortex may follow an age-comparable typical pattern without the proposed atypical elevation; no single connection determines diagnosis.
connection_names: Left Thalamus — Left Superior Temporal Gyrus, anterior division
Right Thalamus — Right Middle Temporal Gyrus, anterior division
Right Thalamus — Right Inferior Temporal Gyrus, anterior division

hypotheses.asd: ASD hypothesis: Thalamic coupling with medial frontal, paracingulate or frontal-opercular cortex may depart from a typical reference in either direction, depending on developmental and network context.
hypotheses.td: TD hypothesis: Thalamic coupling with medial frontal, paracingulate or frontal-opercular cortex may be compatible with a matched typical reference; neither stronger nor weaker coupling alone is decisive.
connection_names: Left Thalamus — Right Frontal Medial Cortex
Right Thalamus — Left Paracingulate Gyrus
Right Thalamus — Left Frontal Operculum Cortex

hypotheses.asd: ASD hypothesis: Anterior-to-posterior default-mode-related functional coupling, including medial frontal to precuneus connections, may be reduced in some autistic individuals relative to matched controls.
hypotheses.td: TD hypothesis: Anterior-to-posterior default-mode-related functional coupling may be consistent with a matched typical developmental reference rather than the proposed reduction.
connection_names: Right Frontal Pole — Left Cingulate Gyrus, posterior division
Left Frontal Medial Cortex — Left Precuneous Cortex

hypotheses.asd: ASD hypothesis: Frontal-to-angular or paracingulate functional coupling may display a non-typical pattern within default-mode-related associative circuitry, without a universal increase or decrease.
hypotheses.td: TD hypothesis: Frontal-to-angular or paracingulate functional coupling may be broadly compatible with an age-matched typical pattern; this association-network profile is not a diagnostic rule.
connection_names: Left Frontal Pole — Right Angular Gyrus
Left Superior Frontal Gyrus — Left Angular Gyrus
Left Angular Gyrus — Left Paracingulate Gyrus

hypotheses.asd: ASD hypothesis: Functional interaction between temporal association cortex and frontal or paracingulate regions may be reduced in social-cognitive circuits; the available parcels are only anatomical proxies.
hypotheses.td: TD hypothesis: Functional interaction between temporal association cortex and frontal or paracingulate regions may follow matched typical patterns; these atlas parcels are not exact study seeds.
connection_names: Left Frontal Pole — Right Middle Temporal Gyrus, posterior division
Right Middle Temporal Gyrus, anterior division — Left Paracingulate Gyrus

hypotheses.asd: ASD hypothesis: Precuneus-to-superior-parietal or superior-frontal connectivity may be relatively reduced in a subset of autistic individuals, suggesting altered posterior associative integration.
hypotheses.td: TD hypothesis: Precuneus-to-superior-parietal or superior-frontal connectivity may follow a matched typical distribution without the proposed associative decoupling.
connection_names: Right Superior Frontal Gyrus — Left Precuneous Cortex
Right Superior Parietal Lobule — Left Precuneous Cortex

hypotheses.asd: ASD hypothesis: Connectivity involving insular, frontal-opercular and supramarginal regions may be atypical in salience or attention-related processing, with subject-dependent direction.
hypotheses.td: TD hypothesis: Connectivity involving insular, frontal-opercular and supramarginal regions may remain within matched typical variation, without asserting that the network is always normal.
connection_names: Right Insular Cortex — Right Frontal Operculum Cortex
Left Insular Cortex — Left Inferior Frontal Gyrus, pars triangularis
Left Insular Cortex — Left Supramarginal Gyrus, posterior division

hypotheses.asd: ASD hypothesis: Inter-network coupling involving insula, posterior cingulate and nearby temporoparietal regions may be unusually coordinated or segregated in autism; test both directions.
hypotheses.td: TD hypothesis: Inter-network coupling involving insula, posterior cingulate and nearby temporoparietal regions may be compatible with a matched typical network balance.
connection_names: Left Insular Cortex — Right Cingulate Gyrus, posterior division
Left Supramarginal Gyrus, posterior division — Left Cingulate Gyrus, posterior division

hypotheses.asd: ASD hypothesis: Resting-state coupling between inferior frontal and temporal language-related regions may be atypical in either direction; task-evoked connectivity directions must not be assumed.
hypotheses.td: TD hypothesis: Resting-state coupling between inferior frontal and temporal language-related regions may align with matched typical variation, without inferring language skill from one edge.
connection_names: Left Inferior Frontal Gyrus, pars triangularis — Left Temporal Pole
Left Inferior Frontal Gyrus, pars triangularis — Left Middle Temporal Gyrus, posterior division
Right Inferior Frontal Gyrus, pars opercularis — Right Superior Temporal Gyrus, posterior division
Right Inferior Frontal Gyrus, pars opercularis — Left Middle Temporal Gyrus, temporooccipital part

hypotheses.asd: ASD hypothesis: Functional coupling across superior temporal, Heschl and planum temporale regions may reflect atypical auditory-association network integration, with no fixed direction.
hypotheses.td: TD hypothesis: Functional coupling across superior temporal, Heschl and planum temporale regions may be compatible with the matched typical auditory-association profile.
connection_names: Left Superior Temporal Gyrus, anterior division — Right Heschl's Gyrus (includes H1 and H2)
Left Superior Temporal Gyrus, anterior division — Left Heschl's Gyrus (includes H1 and H2)
Left Superior Temporal Gyrus, anterior division — Right Planum Temporale
Left Central Opercular Cortex — Left Heschl's Gyrus (includes H1 and H2)

hypotheses.asd: ASD hypothesis: Corticostriatal coupling between caudate and frontal or motor-associated cortex may be atypical, but its direction and location may differ across individuals.
hypotheses.td: TD hypothesis: Corticostriatal coupling between caudate and frontal or motor-associated cortex may be consistent with a matched typical reference, not a universal rule.
connection_names: Left Caudate — Right Superior Frontal Gyrus
Right Caudate — Right Inferior Frontal Gyrus, pars opercularis
Right Caudate — Right Juxtapositional Lobule Cortex (formerly Supplementary Motor Cortex)

hypotheses.asd: ASD hypothesis: Selected sensorimotor-to-parietal or premotor connections may show reduced coordination as part of a broader sensory and attention hypoconnectivity pattern.
hypotheses.td: TD hypothesis: Selected sensorimotor-to-parietal or premotor connections may be compatible with matched typical coordination rather than the proposed reduction.
connection_names: Left Putamen — Left Postcentral Gyrus
Right Postcentral Gyrus — Right Juxtapositional Lobule Cortex (formerly Supplementary Motor Cortex)
Left Postcentral Gyrus — Right Superior Parietal Lobule
Left Superior Parietal Lobule — Left Juxtapositional Lobule Cortex (formerly Supplementary Motor Cortex)

hypotheses.asd: ASD hypothesis: Functional coupling between temporal association and inferior parietal regions may be atypical in social-information integration, but direction cannot be fixed from the literature.
hypotheses.td: TD hypothesis: Functional coupling between temporal association and inferior parietal regions may follow matched typical patterns; atypicality cannot be diagnosed from one pair.
connection_names: Right Superior Temporal Gyrus, anterior division — Right Supramarginal Gyrus, anterior division
Left Middle Temporal Gyrus, anterior division — Right Supramarginal Gyrus, anterior division
Right Middle Temporal Gyrus, posterior division — Left Angular Gyrus
Right Supramarginal Gyrus, anterior division — Right Angular Gyrus

hypotheses.asd: Exploratory ASD hypothesis: Amygdala-to-temporal and supramarginal functional coupling might vary with social-affective integration; no direction or diagnostic specificity is established here.
hypotheses.td: Exploratory TD hypothesis: Amygdala-to-temporal and supramarginal functional coupling might remain within broad typical variation; evidence for exact-edge diagnosis is insufficient.

hypotheses.asd: Exploratory ASD hypothesis: Cross-modal auditory, somatomotor and occipital-to-precuneus coupling may depart from typical patterns in some cases; motion-related alternatives must be evaluated.
hypotheses.td: Exploratory TD hypothesis: Cross-modal auditory, somatomotor and occipital-to-precuneus coupling may be compatible with quality-matched typical connectivity patterns.

hypotheses.asd: Exploratory ASD hypothesis: Medial frontal, cingulate and paracingulate connectivity may be atypical within control and salience-related circuitry; direction is uncertain at these exact parcels.
hypotheses.td: Exploratory TD hypothesis: Medial frontal, cingulate and paracingulate connectivity may be compatible with a matched typical reference, without overinterpreting one parcel.
